rules: Change the title in the HTML the server sends, on the test pages only, on the same URLs.
Leave the control pages, their internal links and the rest of the template untouched until the read-out.
Check Google's Search Status Dashboard before launch and note any ranking update that starts during the test.
Seven days after launch, inspect the test pages; the test window starts the Monday after 80% show a crawl after launch.

contamination.source: your note; WordPress isn't connected, so modified dates of the other pages weren't checked

effects.formula: (test window - test baseline) - (control window - control baseline); negative means test moved up

without_a_control.reading: On their own, the test pages went down 1.3% in clicks a week, which looks like a failed change. The control pages fell 10.4% and the whole site 9.3% over the same weeks, so the season pulled everything down; against the control, the titles added 10.2% clicks.

ga4_secondary.note: Information only. Organic sessions on the test pages ran 11.5% against control (real); key events -14.7% (noise: the gap of 25.8 is inside the threshold of 26.4). GA4 counts fewer visits than Search Console counts clicks, so the two are never mixed.

verdict.summary: The new titles lifted clicks by 10.2% (95% interval 4.2% to 16.5%), through CTR (9.8%) rather than impressions (0.4%, interval -1.7% to 2.5%).
verdict.next_step: Roll the new title out to the 22 control pages (the edited page included), then judge the rollout in 4 weeks against another section of the site. WordPress isn't connected, so here are the titles to paste.
